title: Age-related changes in performance and recovery kinetics in masters athletes: a narrative review
authors: Borges N, Reaburn P, Driller M, Argus C
journal: Journal of Aging and Physical Activity
population: Masters athletes; review of performance and recovery literature
findings: Current research suggests the effect of age on performance and recovery may be smaller than originally suggested, and increasing sedentary lifestyles appear to play a larger role in observed decrements.
Performance decrements appear inevitable with age, but performance capacities can be maintained through systematic physical training.
The limited current research suggests there may be an age effect on recovery kinetics following an exercise bout; acute and chronic recovery processes in the masters athlete need further research.
limitations: Narrative review; authors state evidence on recovery kinetics is limited. No quantitative effect sizes in the abstract. This is the Borges review (2016); the 2018 Borges paper in this corpus is an experiment, not a review.
implications: Do not hard-code a large age-based recovery penalty; allow a small, adjustable recovery-demand factor for masters athletes (start at default spacing and let readiness data lengthen it).
Keep training consistency the primary lever and avoid prescribing long unplanned breaks, since inactivity rather than age is the main driver of observed decline in this review.

verification.notes: Crossref and Europe PMC abstract match; all three findings stated in the abstract. Year 2016 in Crossref (issue year).
